subject: common shrew
title: This Animal Shrinks Its Own Skull Every Winter, Then Regrows It

scenes.text: Every winter, this tiny animal shrinks its own skull.
In one study, the common shrew's braincase shrank about 15 percent over the winter.
Its brain shrinks too, and so does the rest of its body.
A 2025 brain-scan study found the brain loses water, about nine percent of its volume.
And the brain cells don't die. Less tissue simply costs less energy to feed through the cold.
Then spring comes, and the skull grows back, almost to full size. A smaller head, on purpose.

description:
The common shrew shrinks its skull and brain every winter, then regrows them in spring: Dehnel's phenomenon.
Tracking wild shrews, researchers measured the braincase shrinking by about 15 percent in winter and rebounding almost fully in spring (Current Biology, 2017). A 2025 MRI study found the brain loses about nine percent of its volume through water loss, without brain cells dying. A smaller brain is cheaper to run when food is scarce.
Which animal survival trick is the strangest?
first_comment: Weasels and some moles show the same winter shrinking. Would you trade a smaller brain for a warmer winter?
